summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic abdominal pain localized near her gastrostomy tube site, three days after a prior discharge. The pain was focal and tender on examination with a positive Carnett’s sign, suggesting abdominal wall musculature as the source. Imaging showed a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern and gaseous distention of the stomach, likely related to her complex surgical history, but no evidence of infection or free air. Tube feeds were held overnight and successfully restarted. Gabapentin was increased to 600 mg TID for improved pain control, and she continued erythromycin and rifaximin for bacterial overgrowth. Mild leukopenia improved without intervention. She met with a social worker, discussed coping strategies, and was discharged home with stable pain, a plan to follow up with her GI doctor, and instructions to repeat CBC in one week.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Decreased white blood cell count, unspecified
